legend: Do you believe in alternative worlds? A group of researchers has discovered an anomaly that may indicate the existence of parallel realities. To confirm or refute the theory, they need to solve the following problem:

You are given a multiset a%%ZSMJ0%% consisting of numbers a1,⋯,an%%ZSMJ1%%. It is required to split it into some collection of non-empty multisets S1,⋯,Sk%%ZSMJ2%% so as to maximize the sum of their medians.

In other words, you need to choose the number of multisets k%%ZSMJ3%% and assign each element of the multiset a%%ZSMJ4%% to exactly one of the sets S1,⋯,Sk%%ZSMJ5%%. Then you need to compute x=med(S1)+med(S2)+⋯+med(Sk)%%ZSMJ6%%.
As the answer, you need to find the maximum possible value of x%%ZSMJ7%%.
In this problem, for a sorted set S%%ZSMJ8%% with elements s1,⋯,sm%%ZSMJ9%% (arranged in increasing order), the median is defined as follows: med(S)=(s⌈n2⌉+s⌈n+12⌉)/2%%ZSMJ10%%.
input: The first line of the input contains the number n%%ZSMJ13%% (1≤n≤3⋅105%%ZSMJ14%%).
The second line contains n%%ZSMJ15%% integers a1,a2,…,an(|ai|≤109)%%ZSMJ16%% — the values of the elements of the multiset a%%ZSMJ17%%.
output: In the only line, print the answer to the problem, multiplied by 2%%ZSMJ18%%.
